title: Caddy Server Running for 3-4 weeks, and then all requests fail

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
That's odd. First thing to do would be to grab a CPU profile while it's unresponsive. At `localhost:2019/debug/pprof` on the server you can access links to collect a CPU profile (if you add `?seconds=10` or something to the URL it'll take a profile over time).

Without a profile we'll just be guessing. A goroutine dump could be useful too.

Is there a particular request that triggers this behavior?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
No request in particular. So far it just seems to happen after a certain amount of time.

Is there any way to grab the dump externally? I assume not, as I assume that wouldn't be secure. Since it's running externally on a docker-container host, I'm not sure if I have the ability to access it from localhost.

Is there a way I can expose this externally under a different endpoint? I've noticed that bots will preemptively call `/debug/pprof` on some of my other servers, looking for holes. If I can hide it behind a secret uuid endpoint, that'd allow me to access it easily the next time this happens.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> I assume not, as I assume that wouldn't be secure. 

The debug/pprof endpoint does not actually have security sensitive information, it just so happens that we stuck it on the admin listener since that made the most sense... you could in theory open up the admin endpoint if you can't get into localhost... as long as you either enable authentication OR specify a listener that is still internal-only.

Use the `admin` global option to set the listener address to something that's still an internal interface and then you won't need authentication (probably): https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/options#admin

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: I should mention, the `respond /ping 200` won't even respond when this happens. Why would this other endpoint respond?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Really depends on the nature of the bug.  Give it a few minutes to respond and see what happens.

In the meantime, could you post the logs here, and also enable debug logging (`debug` in your global options)? That will give us more insight.

For example, if you get a flood of requests, you're simply getting DoS'ed. A firewall or CDN can help with that.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Yes, please upgrade to the latest version, v2.7.4. See https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/releases. You can subscribe to be notified for releases by clicking Watch then choose Custom to only get alerts for releases.

I don't think we'll learn anything from letting it "fail" on an older version. We've fixed _lots_ of issues since, and without more evidence, it's impossible to rule out that it hasn't already been fixed.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Thanks for the charts.

I believe it is happening, which is about all I can glean from charts, though.

> 119054 GET requests per hour during 32 days should do it

We'd have to reproduce these requests :sweat: 

What we _really need_ is either a way to reproduce it or a profile captured during the event. Debug logs may be helpful too -- especially with #5793 -- but the profile will tell us where in the code the CPU use is coming from. Logs mainly add context.

My first reply above has some instructions for grabbing a profile. This can also be done on a regular basis if you don't want to supervise it. Just dump the profiles somewhere and after it happens, go find the profile that happened during the event. That would be very helpful!
